name: Largest & Second Largest Element in Array
notes: Single-pass tracking: largest and second largest. Edge case: all elements equal.

name: Check if Array Is Sorted and Rotated
notes: Count transitions where nums[i] > nums[(i+1)%n]. If count <= 1, then true.

name: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
notes: Slow pointer i holds unique index, fast pointer j scans. nums[i+1] = nums[j] when different.

name: Move Zeroes to End
notes: First find index of first zero, then swap non-zero elements into it.

name: Single Number (Find element appearing once)
notes: XOR all elements. X ^ X = 0, X ^ 0 = X.

name: Missing Number in Range [0, n]
notes: Expected sum n*(n+1)//2 - actual sum, or XOR range with actual numbers.

name: Two Sum (Return Indices)
notes: Map: num -> index. Check if target - num exists. O(N) time, O(N) space.

name: Majority Element (> n/2 occurrences)
notes: Candidate & count. If count == 0, new candidate. Same -> +1, diff -> -1. O(1) space.

name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock I
notes: Track min_price so far, compute potential profit = price - min_price, update max_profit.

name: Leaders in an Array
notes: Traverse from right to left maintaining maximum element seen so far.

name: Rotate Array by K Places to Right
notes: k %= n. Reverse first n-k, reverse last k, reverse entire array. O(1) space.

name: Union of Two Sorted Arrays
notes: Merge two pointers while skipping duplicates before adding to result.

name: Longest Subarray with Sum K (Positives + Negatives)
notes: PrefixSum map storing earliest index. If (curr_sum - K) in map, len = i - map[curr_sum - K].

name: Sort Colors (Sort 0s, 1s, and 2s)
notes: 3 Pointers: low, mid, high. 0s to left of low, 2s to right of high. Single pass O(N).

name: Maximum Subarray Sum
notes: curr_sum = max(x, curr_sum + x). Track max_so_far. Also practice printing the subarray indices.

name: Rearrange Array Elements by Sign
notes: Positives at even indices (0, 2, 4..), negatives at odd indices (1, 3, 5..).

name: Next Permutation
notes: Find pivot from right: a[i] < a[i+1]. Swap with next greater element to right, then reverse suffix.

name: Longest Consecutive Sequence
notes: Put in HashSet. Only start counting sequence if (num - 1) is NOT in set. O(N) total.

name: Set Matrix Zeroes
notes: Use 1st row & 1st col as marker arrays + col0 boolean variable for O(1) space.

name: Rotate Image (Rotate Matrix 90 degrees Clockwise)
notes: Transpose matrix (swap matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i]), then reverse each row. In-place.

name: Spiral Matrix Traversal
notes: Maintain 4 boundaries: top, bottom, left, right. Traverse edges and shrink boundaries.

name: Subarray Sum Equals K
notes: Map: prefix_sum -> frequency. Initialize map[0] = 1. Add map[curr_sum - k] to answer.

name: Pascal's Triangle
notes: Learn 3 variations: find element at (r, c) = (r-1)C(c-1), print nth row, generate full triangle.

name: Majority Element II (> n/3 occurrences)
notes: At most 2 elements can occur > n/3 times. Track 2 candidates and 2 counters, then verify.

name: 3-Sum
notes: Sort array. Fix first element i, run two pointers (j, k) for remainder. Skip duplicate values.

name: 4-Sum
notes: Sort array. Fix i and j, use two pointers for k and l. Beware of integer overflow in sums.

name: Merge Overlapping Subintervals
notes: Sort intervals by start time. If current start <= previous end, merge (prev.end = max). Else new interval.

name: Merge Two Sorted Arrays Without Extra Space
notes: Leetcode: fill from end (m+n-1). In-place GFG: Gap method (Shell sort logic) ceil(gap/2).

name: Find Missing and Repeating Number
notes: Equations: S - Sn = x - y and S2 - S2n = x^2 - y^2. Or XOR grouping with rightmost set bit.

name: Maximum Product Subarray
notes: Compute prefix and suffix products. If product is 0, reset to 1. Track global maximum.

name: Subarray Sums Divisible by K
notes: Prefix sum % k. Maintain frequency map of remainders. (rem + k) % k to handle negative numbers.

name: Spiral Matrix II (Generate Matrix)
notes: Fill matrix sequentially from 1 to n^2 by tracking top, bottom, left, and right bounds.

name: Container With Most Water
notes: Pointers at both ends. Area = (r - l) * min(h[l], h[r]). Always move the pointer with smaller height.

name: Merge Sort Algorithm from Scratch
notes: Divide at mid, recursively sort left and right, merge with two pointers. Time: O(N log N), Space: O(N).

name: Quick Sort Algorithm (Hoare & Lomuto Partition)
notes: Pick pivot, partition such that elements <= pivot are left, elements > pivot are right. In-place, O(N log N) avg.

name: Subarrays with Given XOR K
notes: xr = prefix_xor. xr ^ k is required. Count += map[xr ^ k]. map[xr]++.

name: Count Inversions in an Array
notes: In merge step: if arr[left] > arr[right], count += (mid - left + 1) because all left are sorted.

name: Reverse Pairs (nums[i] > 2*nums[j])
notes: Count valid pairs right before merging each halved array in merge sort. O(N log N).

name: Week 1 Hard Review: Next Permutation & Reverse Pairs
notes: Re-code from scratch without looking: 1) Next Permutation 2) Subarray Sum Equals K 3) Reverse Pairs.

name: Binary Search in Sorted Array
notes: mid = low + (high - low)//2 to prevent integer overflow. O(log N).

name: Implement Lower Bound and Upper Bound
notes: Lower Bound: smallest index where arr[idx] >= x. Upper Bound: arr[idx] > x.

name: Search Insert Position
notes: Directly equal to finding the Lower Bound index of target in sorted array.

name: Count Occurrences in Sorted Array
notes: Count = (last_pos - first_pos + 1) if present, else 0.

name: Square Root & Nth Root of Integer
notes: Search range [1, N]. If mid*mid <= n, record mid and search right.

name: First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
notes: Run two separate binary searches: one biasing left (high = mid-1), one biasing right (low = mid+1).

name: Search in Rotated Sorted Array I (Unique Elements)
notes: At least one half (left or right) is always sorted. Check if target lies in sorted half.

name: Search in Rotated Sorted Array II (With Duplicates)
notes: When arr[low] == arr[mid] == arr[high], shrink search space: low++, high--.

name: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
notes: If arr[low] <= arr[high], min is arr[low]. Else eliminate sorted half after recording its min.

name: Single Element in a Sorted Array
notes: Left of single element: (even, odd) index pairs match. Right: (odd, even) match. Check mid parity.

name: Find Peak Element
notes: If arr[mid] > arr[mid+1], peak lies on left (including mid). Else peak lies on right.

name: Koko Eating Bananas
notes: Search speed k in [1, max(piles)]. Predicate: sum(ceil(pile/k)) <= h. Find minimum feasible k.

name: Minimum Days to Make M Bouquets
notes: Day range [min(bloomDay), max(bloomDay)]. Count consecutive bloomed flowers / k.

name: Capacity to Ship Packages within D Days
notes: Capacity range [max(weights), sum(weights)]. Greedily pack until exceeding capacity.

name: Search a 2D Matrix I (Strictly Sorted)
notes: Flatten virtual 1D index: row = mid // cols, col = mid % cols. Standard BS in [0, m*n - 1].

name: Search a 2D Matrix II (Rows & Columns Sorted)
notes: Start at top-right corner (0, cols-1). If val > target col--, else if val < target row++. O(M+N).

name: Aggressive Cows (Distance Maximization)
notes: Sort stalls. Binary search minimum distance d in [1, max - min]. Greedily place cows.

name: Book Allocation Problem / Split Array Largest Sum
notes: Range [max(pages), sum(pages)]. Predicate: can we allocate to <= m students? Find min capacity.

name: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
notes: BS on smaller array partition cut1 in [0, n1]. Check l1 <= r2 and l2 <= r1. O(log(min(N, M))).

name: K-th Element of Two Sorted Arrays
notes: Same as median partition cut, but cut1 in [max(0, k-m), min(k, n)].

name: Find Peak Element in 2D Matrix
notes: Pick mid column, find row with max element in that column. Compare with left & right neighbors.

name: Matrix Median in Row-Wise Sorted Matrix
notes: BS range [min_elem, max_elem]. For mid, count elements <= mid across all rows using upper_bound. Find median count (R*C+1)//2.

name: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
notes: Map: char -> last seen index. When duplicate seen, jump left = max(left, map[c] + 1).

name: Max Consecutive Ones III (Flip K Zeroes)
notes: Maintain window with at most k zeroes. If zeroes > k, increment left pointer.

name: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
notes: Window length - max_freq <= k. Track max_freq in window. O(N) single pass.

name: Binary Subarrays With Sum & Nice Subarrays
notes: Golden pattern: count(sum == k) = countAtMost(k) - countAtMost(k-1). Reduces to sliding window!

name: Fruit Into Baskets
notes: Equivalent to Longest Subarray with at most 2 distinct characters. Hash map of counts.

name: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
notes: Expand right until sum >= target, then shrink left to find minimal window length.

name: Number of Substrings Containing All Three Characters (a, b, c)
notes: Track last seen index of 'a', 'b', 'c'. Valid substrings ending at i is 1 + min(last_a, last_b, last_c).

name: Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards
notes: Start with left sum of first k cards. Shift window: subtract card from left, add card from right.

name: Count Number of Substrings with Exactly K Distinct Characters
notes: Count exactly K distinct = atMost(K) - atMost(K-1). Each atMost is standard sliding window.

name: Subarrays with K Different Integers
notes: Compute exactlyK(nums, k) = atMostK(nums, k) - atMostK(nums, k-1). Each atMost is standard O(N).

name: Minimum Window Substring
notes: Track required character counts. Once count == 0, shrink from left while valid to find minimal length.

name: Reverse a Linked List (Iterative & Recursive)
notes: Iterative: prev = None, curr = head, next_node = curr.next, curr.next = prev. Master recursive too.

name: Middle of the Linked List
notes: slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2 steps. When fast or fast.next is None, slow is at middle.

name: Detect Loop in Linked List
notes: If fast and slow pointers meet, cycle exists. If fast reaches None, no cycle.

name: Intersection Point of Two Linked Lists
notes: p1 = p1.next if p1 else headB; p2 = p2.next if p2 else headA. They meet at intersection in 2 passes!

name: Longest Common Prefix
notes: Sort strings and compare only first and last string, or scan horizontally character by character.

name: Isomorphic Strings
notes: Two maps: s->t and t->s to ensure one-to-one mapping (bijection). Same length requirement.

name: Valid Anagram
notes: Array of size 26. Increment for s, decrement for t. Check all values are 0.

name: Reverse a Doubly Linked List
notes: For every node, swap node.next and node.prev. Move curr = curr.prev (since pointers are swapped).

name: Find Pairs with Given Sum in Sorted DLL
notes: Left pointer at head, right pointer at tail. If sum < target left = left.next; else right = right.prev. O(N).

name: Remove Duplicates from Sorted DLL
notes: Track next_unique node. Adjust curr.next = next_unique and next_unique.prev = curr. Free skipped nodes.

name: Find Starting Point of Loop in Linked List
notes: When slow and fast meet, reset slow to head. Advance both 1 step at a time; meeting node is start!

name: Check if Linked List is Palindrome
notes: Find middle, reverse second half, compare first and second half, restore second half.

name: Remove Nth Node from End of List
notes: Use dummy node. Advance fast pointer by N steps ahead. Then move both until fast reaches end.

name: Odd Even Linked List
notes: Maintain odd and even pointers + evenHead. Link odd.next = odd.next.next. In the end, odd.next = evenHead.

name: Sort a Linked List
notes: Find middle with slow/fast (break link: mid.next = None), sort left and right recursively, merge sorted lists.

name: Add Two Numbers Represented as Linked Lists
notes: Iterate while l1, l2 or carry > 0. val = (l1.val + l2.val + carry) % 10, carry = sum // 10.

name: Copy List with Random Pointer
notes: Step 1: Create copy nodes and insert between originals. Step 2: Assign copy.random. Step 3: Separate lists.

name: Design LRU Cache
notes: Map: key -> Node. Doubly Linked List with head and tail sentinel nodes. Remove node, insert after head.

name: Rotate List by K Places
notes: Connect tail to head to form ring. Break ring at (len - (k % len))th node.

name: Reverse Words in a String
notes: Trim spaces, split into words, reverse word order, join with single space. Or reverse in-place.

name: Sort Characters by Frequency
notes: Count frequencies. Use bucket sort where bucket[f] stores chars with frequency f. O(N).

name: String to Integer (atoi)
notes: Handle leading spaces, sign (+/-), digit reading with clamping to INT_MIN (-2^31) and INT_MAX (2^31-1).

name: Longest Palindromic Substring
notes: Expand around center for both odd (i, i) and even (i, i+1) centers. O(N^2) time, O(1) space.

name: Sum of Beauty of All Substrings
notes: Beauty = max_freq - min_freq (for non-zero freq chars). Nested loop O(26 * N^2).

name: Repeated String Match
notes: Repeat string A until len(A) >= len(B). Check if B in A; if not, check A + original_A.

name: Swap Nodes in Pairs
notes: Special case of k-group with k=2. Dummy node + pointer manipulation.

name: Reorder List (L0 -> Ln -> L1 -> Ln-1)
notes: Triple pattern integration: 1) Find mid. 2) Reverse second half. 3) Interleave two halves.

name: Delete All Occurrences of a Given Key in DLL
notes: Handle head node deletion carefully (update head = next_node, next_node.prev = None). In-place O(N).

name: Reverse Nodes in K-Group
notes: Check if k nodes exist ahead. If yes, reverse k nodes and link with previous block. Repeat.

name: Flattening a Linked List (Multi-level child)
notes: Recursively merge bottom lists from right to left using standard sorted 2-list merge.

name: Design LFU (Least Frequently Used) Cache
notes: Map: key -> Node, freqMap: freq -> DoublyLinkedList. Track minFreq. Update node frequency on access.

name: Longest Happy Prefix / Find String in String
notes: Build Longest Prefix Suffix (LPS) array in O(N). lps[n-1] gives length of longest proper prefix=suffix.

name: Shortest Palindrome (Add chars in front)
notes: Combine s + '#' + reverse(s). Compute LPS array. Missing palindrome suffix = s[lps[-1]:]. Reverse & prepend.

name: Z-Algorithm for Pattern Search & Rabin-Karp
notes: Rabin-Karp uses rolling hash. Modulo arithmetic to prevent overflow. Verify hash collision.

name: Week 3 Mastery Check: LRU Cache & K-Group Reversal
notes: Code LRU Cache and Reverse K-group on a blank whiteboard / LeetCode scratchpad without looking at notes.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Valid Parentheses
notes: Push opening brackets. On closing bracket, match with stack.top() and pop. Stack must be empty at end.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Implement Queue using Stacks (Amortized O(1))
notes: Two stacks: input and output. Push to input. Pop from output; if output empty, pour all from input to output.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Next Greater Element I
notes: Traverse from right. Pop while stack.top() <= num. nge[num] = stack.top() if stack else -1. Push num.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Bit Manipulation Fundamentals (Check, Set, Clear, Toggle)
notes: Check: (n >> i) & 1. Set: n | (1 << i). Clear: n & ~(1 << i). Toggle: n ^ (1 << i).

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Number of 1 Bits & Power of Two Check
notes: n & (n - 1) removes the lowest set bit. Power of 2: n > 0 and (n & (n - 1)) == 0.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Find GCD / HCF in O(log(min(a, b)))
notes: Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b). Stop when b == 0. LCM = (a * b) // gcd(a, b).

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Implement Min Stack in O(1) Time & Space
notes: O(1) space trick: push 2*val - minVal when val < minVal. Or store (val, currentMin) pair.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Infix to Postfix Conversion
notes: Operator precedence table. Pop operators with higher or equal precedence before pushing current.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation (Postfix)
notes: Push operands. On operator, pop right operand then left operand, evaluate, push result.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Next Greater Element II (Circular)
notes: Simulate 2*n iterations. Index using i % n. Populate answer array during the second virtual pass.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Sum of Subarray Minimums
notes: For each element, count left subarrays (PSEE) and right subarrays (NSE). Contribution = arr[i] * left * right.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Remove K Digits to Minimize Number
notes: Pop digits from stack while k > 0 and stack.top() > curr_digit. Strip leading zeroes.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Online Stock Span
notes: Stack stores (price, span). Pop while stack.top.price <= price and accumulate spans. Push (price, span).

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Asteroid Collision
notes: Collision only occurs when top is positive and current asteroid is negative. Pop, explode, or survive.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: The Celebrity Problem
notes: Put all people on stack. Pop top 2: if A knows B, A is not celeb; else B is not. Verify final candidate.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Divide Two Integers Without Multiplication or Division
notes: Subtract (divisor << shift) where shift is largest power of 2 such that divisor<<shift <= dividend.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Single Number II (Every element appears 3 times except one)
notes: Sum bits at each of 32 positions mod 3. Or state machine: ones = (ones ^ num) & ~twos.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Single Number III (Two unique elements)
notes: XOR all = x ^ y. Find lowest set bit diff = (xy & -xy). Partition array into two buckets by diff bit.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Power Set (All Subsets using Bits)
notes: Loop mask from 0 to (1 << n) - 1. If (mask & (1 << j)), include nums[j] in subset.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Count Primes (Sieve of Eratosthenes)
notes: Boolean array of size n. Mark multiples of i starting from i*i up to n. O(N log(log N)).

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Pow(x, n) in O(log N)
notes: If n < 0, x = 1/x, n = -n. While n > 0: if n % 2 == 1: ans *= x; x *= x; n //= 2.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Print All Divisors & Prime Factorization using Sieve (SPF)
notes: Compute Smallest Prime Factor spf[x]. Factorize any number in O(log N) by dividing n by spf[n].

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Single Number III & Bitmask Benchmark
notes: Benchmark test: Partition array into two buckets based on lowest set bit diff.

name: Prefix to Infix Conversion
notes: Read prefix from right to left. On operand: push to stack. On operator: pop op1, op2, push '(' + op1 + op + op2 + ')'.
phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation

name: Prefix to Postfix Conversion
notes: Read from right to left. On operator: pop op1, op2, push op1 + op2 + op.
phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation

name: Postfix to Infix Conversion
notes: Read from left to right. On operator: pop op2, op1, push '(' + op1 + op + op2 + ')'.
phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation

name: Postfix to Prefix Conversion
notes: Read from left to right. On operator: pop op2, op1, push op + op1 + op2.
phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation

name: Sum of Subarray Ranges
notes: Range sum = Sum of Subarray Maxima - Sum of Subarray Minima. Solve in two O(N) monotonic stack passes.
phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation

name: Number of NGEs to the Right
notes: Count elements greater than query index to its right. Process offline or via monotonic stack.
phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Trapping Rain Water
notes: Two pointers left=0, right=n-1 with left_max, right_max. Move pointer at smaller max. O(1) space.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
notes: When popping height h from stack, width = i - stack.top() - 1 (or i if stack empty). Max area = h * width.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Maximal Rectangle in 2D Binary Matrix
notes: Compute height histogram for each row (reset to 0 if cell is '0'). Run Largest Rectangle in Histogram on each row.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Sliding Window Maximum
notes: Maintain monotonically decreasing deque of indices. Pop indices outside window [i-k+1, i]. deque[0] is max.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Phase 1-4 Consolidation: Trapping Rainwater & Monotonic Stack
notes: Mid-Point Milestone: Review Monotonic Stack foundations and solve Trapping Rainwater & Histogram from scratch.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Largest Rectangle in Histogram Benchmark
notes: Benchmark test: Re-code histogram in under 15 minutes without reference.

phase: Phase 5: Stacks & Monotonic Queues & Bit Manipulation
name: Sliding Window Maximum Benchmark
notes: Benchmark test: Implement monotonic deque with window index expiration.

name: Generate Parentheses
notes: Backtrack: add '(' if open < n; add ')' if close < open. Stop when len == 2*n.

name: Combination Sum I (Unlimited reuse)
notes: Pick: subtract candidates[i] and call f(i, target - val). Not pick: call f(i+1, target). Base: target == 0.

name: Combination Sum II (Each number used once, unique combinations)
notes: Sort first. In loop: if j > start and arr[j] == arr[j-1]: continue. Prevents duplicate combinations.

name: Subsets II (Unique Subsets with Duplicate Elements)
notes: Sort array. At each level of recursion loop from idx to n: if i > idx and nums[i] == nums[i-1] skip.

name: Palindrome Partitioning
notes: Partition string at index i. If s[start:i+1] is palindrome, add to path and recurse on i+1.

name: Word Search in 2D Board
notes: Check bounds & char match. Mark visited: board[r][c] = '#'. Explore 4 neighbors. Restore char on return.

name: Rat in a Maze Problem
notes: Explore 'D', 'L', 'R', 'U' in alphabetical order. Mark visited matrix to prevent cycles.

name: M-Coloring Problem
notes: Assign colors 1 to M to node. Check if any adjacent node has same color before recursing.

name: Permutations (All orderings of array)
notes: In-place swapping: swap nums[idx] with nums[i], recurse idx+1, backtrack swap back.

name: Word Break I
notes: dp[i] is True if s[:i] can be segmented. For j in [0, i]: if dp[j] and s[j:i] in wordSet -> dp[i] = True.

name: Combination Sum III (K numbers sum to N)
notes: Digits 1-9 used at most once. Pick k numbers that sum to n. Standard loop recursion.

name: N-Queens
notes: Row by row. O(1) safety check using boolean arrays: cols[c], diag1[r+c], diag2[r-c+n-1].

name: Sudoku Solver
notes: Find empty cell '.'. Try digits '1'-'9'. Check row, col, and 3x3 box (3*(r//3) + i//3, 3*(c//3) + i%3). Return True on finish.

name: Expression Add Operators
notes: Manage multiplication precedence: for '*', value = prev_val - prev_mult + prev_mult * curr_num.

name: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
notes: 1 + max(maxDepth(root.left), maxDepth(root.right)). Base case: root is None -> 0.

name: Check if Binary Tree is Balanced
notes: Return -1 from height function if subtree is unbalanced (|lh - rh| > 1). Prevents O(N^2) double calculation.

name: Diameter of Binary Tree
notes: Update global diameter = max(diameter, lh + rh) at every node, while returning 1 + max(lh, rh).

name: Symmetric Tree (Mirror of Itself)
notes: Helper isMirror(t1, t2): check t1.val == t2.val and isMirror(t1.left, t2.right) and isMirror(t1.right, t2.left).

name: Search & Insert in BST
notes: If target < node.val go left; if target > node.val go right. O(H) time complexity.

name: Same Tree / Check if Two Trees are Identical
notes: If both None: True. If one None or values differ: False. Return isSame(p.left, q.left) and isSame(p.right, q.right).

name: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal (BFS)
notes: Queue storing nodes. For each level, size = q.size(). Pop size elements and push children.

name: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
notes: Maintain leftToRight boolean flag. Insert values into level array from start or end based on flag.

name: Boundary Traversal of Binary Tree
notes: 1. Left boundary (excluding leaves). 2. All leaf nodes (inorder DFS). 3. Right boundary in reverse.

name: Top View & Bottom View of Binary Tree
notes: BFS with line coordinate x. Top view: store line in map only if not already seen. Bottom view: always overwrite!

name: Right / Left View of Binary Tree
notes: Reverse preorder traversal (root, right, left). If depth == len(res), append node.val.

name: Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) in Binary Tree
notes: If root is None or root == p or root == q: return root. If both left and right return non-null, root is LCA!

name: Maximum Width of Binary Tree
notes: Assign index to each node: left child = 2*idx + 1, right child = 2*idx + 2. Subtract min_idx per level.

name: All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree
notes: Map each node to its parent pointer via BFS. Run second BFS starting from target node up to distance K.

name: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder & Inorder
notes: Preorder gives root. Find root in Inorder map to partition into left and right subtrees. O(N).

name: Count Complete Tree Nodes in O((log N)^2)
notes: Compare left height and right height. If equal: (1 << h) - 1. If not, 1 + count(left) + count(right).

name: Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List
notes: Morris traversal or reverse postorder (right, left, root) keeping prev pointer.

name: Preorder, Inorder, and Postorder in One Traversal
notes: Stack of pair (node, state 1/2/3). 1: Preorder, push left. 2: Inorder, push right. 3: Postorder, pop.

name: Delete Node in a BST
notes: Case 1: Leaf. Case 2: 1 child. Case 3: 2 children -> replace with inorder successor (min of right subtree).

name: K-th Smallest Element in a BST
notes: Inorder traversal of BST yields sorted values in ascending order! Decrement k at each visit; return when k==0.

name: Floor and Ceil in a Binary Search Tree
notes: Ceil: if val >= key, ceil = val and move left. Floor: if val <= key, floor = val and move right.

name: Validate Binary Search Tree
notes: Pass valid range (min_val, max_val). Check min_val < node.val < max_val. Recurse left and right.

name: Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST
notes: If both p and q < root.val, go left. If both > root.val, go right. Otherwise, root is the split point (LCA)!

name: Recover Binary Search Tree (Two Nodes Swapped)
notes: Inorder traversal. First violation: prev > curr (first = prev, middle = curr). Second: prev > curr (last = curr). Swap.

name: Binary Search Tree Iterator
notes: Stack pushAllLeft(root). next() pops node and pushes all left descendants of node.right. Amortized O(1).

name: Two Sum IV - Input is a BST
notes: Use two BST Iterators (one forward for ascending, one reverse for descending). Two pointer scan in O(H) space!

name: Construct Binary Tree from Postorder & Inorder
notes: Postorder last element is root. Inorder hashmap partitions left and right subtrees. Recursively build right then left.

name: Inorder Successor & Predecessor in BST
notes: Successor: if curr.val > key: succ = curr, go left. Else: go right. O(H) time, O(1) auxiliary space!

name: Root to Node Path in Binary Tree
notes: DFS: append node.val to path. If node.val == target return True. If left or right finds target, return True. Else pop and return False.

name: Children Sum Property in Binary Tree
notes: If sum(children) < node.val: set children values to node.val. Recurse down. Backtrack: set node.val = sum(children). O(N).

name: Construct BST from Preorder Traversal
notes: Pass upper_bound. If curr val > bound or index == len: return None. root = Node(val), build left (bound=val), build right (bound=bound). O(N).

name: Path Sum II (Root-to-Leaf Paths with Given Sum)
notes: DFS: add node.val to current path. If leaf and target == node.val: record path copy. Backtrack: pop node.val.

name: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
notes: left_gain = max(0, maxPath(node.left)). Global max = max(max_sum, node.val + left_gain + right_gain).

name: Vertical Order Traversal of a Binary Tree
notes: Track (x, y, val) coordinate for each node. Group by column x, then sort by row y, then value.

name: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
notes: Serialize: BFS string with commas and '#' for nulls. Deserialize: split string, queue up nodes, assign left/right.

name: Week 5 Mastery Check: LCA, Tree Max Path Sum & Morris Traversal
notes: Learn Morris Inorder Traversal (threaded binary tree, O(1) space). Review LCA and distance K logic.

name: Morris Traversal for Inorder & Preorder (O(1) Space)
notes: Find rightmost node of left subtree. Create thread to curr. When revisiting, remove thread.

name: Largest BST in Binary Tree
notes: Postorder returns (is_bst, size, min_val, max_val). Check left.max < node.val < right.min.

name: Merge Two BSTs into Balanced BST / Sorted List
pattern: BST to DLL to Balanced BST
notes: Convert both BSTs to sorted lists (or DLLs) in O(M+N). Merge sorted lists. Build balanced BST from sorted array.

name: Burning Tree / Minimum Time to Burn Binary Tree
notes: Map child -> parent using BFS. Start radial BFS from target node. Track burn time using visited set. O(N) time.

name: Maximum Sum BST in Binary Tree
notes: Postorder returns (is_bst, sum_val, min_val, max_val). If left and right are valid BSTs and left.max < root.val < right.min: update global max sum.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: BFS & DFS Traversal of Graph
notes: BFS uses Queue + visited array. DFS uses Recursion / Stack + visited array. Time: O(V + 2E).

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Flood Fill Algorithm
notes: If image[sr][sc] == newColor return. Recurse in 4 directions updating pixel color.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Number of Provinces / Connected Components
notes: Count number of times BFS/DFS is initiated from an unvisited node.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Rotting Oranges
notes: Push all initially rotten oranges into Queue simultaneously (multi-source BFS). Count minutes. Check fresh == 0.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Detect Cycle in Undirected Graph (BFS & DFS)
notes: Store (node, parent) in queue/call stack. If adjacent node is visited and != parent, cycle detected!

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: 0/1 Matrix (Distance to Nearest 0)
notes: Multi-source BFS starting with all 0 cells pushed into queue with dist=0.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Surrounded Regions (Capture O's surrounded by X's)
notes: Start DFS from boundary 'O's and mark them as un-capturable. Then flip remaining 'O's to 'X'.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Is Graph Bipartite?
notes: Color array initialized to -1. Adjacent nodes must have opposite color (0 and 1). Odd-length cycle -> not bipartite.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Course Schedule I & II
notes: Calculate in-degrees. Push 0 in-degree nodes into queue. Decrement neighbors. If count == numCourses -> DAG valid.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Detect Cycle in a Directed Graph (DFS Path Visited)
notes: Two boolean arrays: visited[] and pathVisited[]. If neighbor is currently in pathVisited, cycle exists.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Find Eventual Safe States
notes: Reverse all edges. Terminal nodes now have in-degree 0! Run Kahn's BFS topological sort.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Dijkstra's Shortest Path Algorithm
notes: Min-heap priority queue storing (dist, node). If dist + weight < distTo[neighbor]: relax edge and push.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix & Path with Minimum Effort
notes: Dijkstra min-heap where cost is max(|h1 - h2|) along the path. Relax if current path effort is lower.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
notes: Queue prioritized by number of stops! (stops, node, cost). If stops > k, continue without exploring.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Bellman-Ford & Floyd-Warshall Algorithms
notes: Bellman-Ford relaxes all edges V-1 times (detects negative cycle). Floyd-Warshall computes all-pairs via via-node loop.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Number of Ways to Arrive at Destination
notes: Maintain ways[v]. If new shorter dist found: dist[v] = new_dist, ways[v] = ways[u]. If equal: ways[v] = (ways[v] + ways[u]) % MOD.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Minimum Multiplications to Reach End
notes: Queue storing (steps, num). num = (num * factor) % 100000. Dist array of size 100000.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: City With Smallest Number of Neighbors at Threshold Distance
notes: Run Floyd-Warshall to compute all-pairs shortest distances. Count reachable cities <= threshold.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Disjoint Set Union (DSU) Implementation & Kruskal's MST
notes: findParent(x) with path compression: parent[x] = findParent(parent[x]). unionBySize(u, v). Kruskal sorts edges.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Number of Operations to Make Network Connected
notes: If edges < n-1, impossible. Count redundant edges (both in same component). Answer is (components - 1).

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Accounts Merge
notes: Map each email to account index i. If email already seen, union(i, email_to_node[email]). Group by ultimate parent.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Column
notes: Union row index r with (col index c + offset). Max removed = total_stones - connected_components.

name: Shortest Path in Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)
notes: Compute Topological Sort. Pop nodes from topo order and relax outgoing edges. O(V + E) linear time!
phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms

name: Shortest Path in Undirected Graph with Unit Weights
notes: Standard BFS starting from src with dist[src] = 0. Queue guarantees shortest path for unit weights. O(V + 2E).
phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms

name: Minimum Spanning Tree - Prim's Algorithm
notes: Min-heap storing (weight, node, parent). Pop smallest edge connecting to unvisited node. Add to MST. Mark visited.
phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms

name: Network Delay Time
notes: Dijkstra from source node k. Answer is max(dist) among all nodes. If any node unreachable, return -1.
phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms

name: Number of Enclaves
notes: Start BFS/DFS from boundary land cells (1s) and mark them as connected to outside. Count remaining 1s.
phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms

name: Number of Distinct Islands
notes: Store island coordinates relative to base cell (r - base_r, c - base_c) in HashSet. Set size is distinct islands!
phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms

name: Number of Islands
notes: Iterate all cells. When unvisited '1' found: islands++, run BFS/DFS in 4 directions marking all connected land visited.
phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms

name: Path With Minimum Effort (Dijkstra on Grid)
notes: Min-heap storing (effort, r, c). Effort to neighbor is max(effort, abs(h[nr][nc] - h[r][c])). Stop when destination reached.
phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms

name: Floyd Warshall Algorithm (All-Pairs Shortest Path)
notes: matrix[i][j] = min(matrix[i][j], matrix[i][k] + matrix[k][j]) for each via node k. Detect negative cycles if matrix[i][i] < 0.
phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Alien Dictionary
notes: Compare adjacent words to find first differing char u -> v (directed edge). Run Kahn's topological sort.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Word Ladder I (Shortest Transformation)
notes: Queue storing (word, steps). Try replacing each character with 'a'-'z'. Remove word from HashSet once visited.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Critical Connections in a Network (Bridges in Graph)
notes: Time of insertion tin[] and lowest reachable low[]. If low[neighbor] > tin[node], edge (node, neighbor) is a bridge.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Making A Large Island (Flip at most one 0)
notes: Build DSU on 1s. Then for each 0 cell, sum sizes of unique neighbor island parents + 1. Find global max.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Swim in Rising Water
notes: Dijkstra min-heap where edge cost is max(t, grid[nr][nc]). Find minimum time to reach bottom-right.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Strongly Connected Components (Kosaraju's)
notes: Step 1: Sort by finishing time (DFS push to stack). Step 2: Transpose graph. Step 3: DFS pop stack.

phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms
name: Articulation Point in Graph
notes: Root node is articulation point if children > 1. Non-root is articulation point if low[child] >= tin[node].

name: Word Ladder II (Find All Shortest Transformation Sequences)
notes: Step 1: BFS from startWord to record shortest distance/step of each word. Step 2: Backtrack using DFS from endWord to startWord.
phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms

name: Tarjan's Algorithm for Bridges in Graph
notes: Maintain tin[] and low[]. If low[adj] > tin[node]: edge (node, adj) is a bridge (critical connection)!
phase: Phase 8: Graph Theory & Shortest Path Algorithms

name: Climbing Stairs & Frog Jump
notes: dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]. Frog jump: min(dp[i-1] + abs(h[i]-h[i-1]), dp[i-2] + abs(h[i]-h[i-2])). Space optimize to 2 vars.

name: House Robber I & House Robber II
notes: rob = max(nums[i] + prev2, prev1). House Robber II (circular): max(rob(nums[:-1]), rob(nums[1:])).

name: Ninja's Training
notes: dp[day][last_task] = max over task != last_task (points[day][task] + dp[day-1][task]). Space optimize to size 4 array.

name: Grid Unique Paths I & II (With Obstacles)
notes: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1]. If obstacle at cell, dp[i][j] = 0. Optimize space to 1D row array.

name: Minimum Path Sum in Grid & Triangle
notes: dp[i][j] = grid[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]). Base cases: top and left borders.

name: Subset Sum Equal to Target & Partition Equal Subset Sum
notes: Equal partition = check if subset exists with target = total_sum // 2. dp[target] = dp[target] or dp[target - num].

name: 0/1 Knapsack Problem
notes: dp[w] = max(dp[w], val[i] + dp[w - wt[i]]). Traverse weights backwards from W down to wt[i] for 1D space!

name: Coin Change I (Minimum Coins to Make Sum)
notes: dp[a] = min(dp[a], 1 + dp[a - c]). Initialize with infinity. Traverse forward since coins can be reused unlimited times.

name: Coin Change II & Target Sum
notes: Outer loop over coins, inner loop over amounts: dp[a] += dp[a - coin]. Avoids permutations, counts combinations.

name: Rod Cutting Problem
notes: dp[len] = max(dp[len], price[i] + dp[len - (i+1)]). Standard unbounded knapsack.

name: Week 7 Mastery Check: DSU & Knapsack State Optimization
notes: Contrast 0-1 Knapsack (reverse iteration) vs Unbounded Knapsack (forward iteration). Re-implement DSU.

name: Minimum Falling Path Sum
notes: dp[i][j] = matrix[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j-1], dp[i-1][j], dp[i-1][j+1]). Answer is min of last row.

name: Partitions with Given Difference & Target Sum
notes: s1 - s2 = d and s1 + s2 = total -> s1 = (total + d) // 2. Reduces to count subsets with sum s1!

name: Count Subsets with Sum K
notes: Watch out for array elements equal to 0! Element 0 can be either picked or not picked (factor of 2^zeroes).

name: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS)
notes: If s1[i-1] == s2[j-1]: dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]. Else: max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]). Master printing too!

name: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
notes: Directly equal to LCS(s, reverse(s)). Min insertions to make palindrome = len(s) - LPS(s).

name: Minimum Operations to Convert String A to String B
notes: Deletions = len(s1) - LCS; Insertions = len(s2) - LCS. Total = len(s1) + len(s2) - 2*LCS.

name: Longest Common Substring
notes: Unlike subsequence, reset dp[i][j] = 0 when s1[i-1] != s2[j-1]. Track max value in entire table.

name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II (Unlimited)
notes: buy state = max(prev_buy, prev_sell - price); sell state = max(prev_sell, prev_buy + price).

name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown & Transaction Fee
notes: Cooldown: after sell on day i, can only buy on day i+2. Fee: subtract fee on sell.

name: Longest Increasing Subsequence (O(N log N) BS Method)
notes: Maintain tails array. For each x, binary search (lower_bound) position in tails. If at end, append. Else replace.

name: Largest Divisible Subset & Longest String Chain
notes: Sort array. dp[i] = max(dp[i], 1 + dp[j]) if nums[i] % nums[j] == 0. Maintain hash/parent array to reconstruct subset.

name: Longest Bitonic Subsequence
notes: Compute LIS from left to right (dp1) and LIS from right to left (dp2). Max bitonic length = max(dp1[i] + dp2[i] - 1).

name: Count Square Submatrices with All Ones
notes: dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1]) if matrix[i][j] == 1. Sum of all dp[i][j] is answer!

name: House Robber III (DP on Trees)
notes: Postorder traversal returning (rob_root, skip_root). rob = node.val + left.skip + right.skip; skip = max(left) + max(right).

name: Partition Array for Maximum Sum
notes: Try all partitions of length 1 to k starting at index i: max_elem * len + dp[i + len].

name: Print Longest Common Subsequence
notes: Build LCS table. Backtrack from (m, n): if s1[i-1] == s2[j-1]: append char, i--, j--. Else move toward max cell.

name: Print Longest Increasing Subsequence
notes: dp[i] stores LIS ending at i, hash[i] stores predecessor index. Find max dp[i] and trace back through hash array.

name: Number of Longest Increasing Subsequences
notes: Maintain len[i] and count[i]. If len[j] + 1 > len[i]: len[i] = len[j] + 1, count[i] = count[j]. If equal: count[i] += count[j].

name: Frog Jump with K Distance
notes: dp[i] = min over j in [1, k] (dp[i-j] + abs(height[i] - height[i-j])). O(N*K) time, O(K) space.

name: Unbounded Knapsack Problem
notes: Pick stays on same index: take = val[i] + f(i, W - wt[i]). 1D space optimization: traverse capacity left to right.

name: Minimum Path Sum in Triangular Grid
notes: dp[i][j] = triangle[i][j] + min(dp[i+1][j], dp[i+1][j+1]). Base case: bottom row. Optimize to 1D array of size N.

name: Longest String Chain
notes: Sort strings by length. For each word, generate predecessors by deleting 1 char. dp[word] = max(dp.get(pred, 0) + 1).

name: Cherry Pickup II (Chocolates Pickup)
notes: Both robots move to row i+1 simultaneously. State: dp[r][c1][c2]. Try all 9 combinations of (dc1, dc2) in {-1, 0, 1}.

name: Partition Set into Two Subsets with Min Absolute Sum Difference
notes: Last row of subset sum DP table gives all reachable subset sums. Find s1 minimizing abs(total - 2*s1).

name: Shortest Common Supersequence
notes: Build LCS table. Backtrack from (m, n): if matching, take char once; if unequal, take char from branch that yielded max.

name: Distinct Subsequences (s contains t)
notes: If s[i-1] == t[j-1]: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + dp[i-1][j]. Else dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j]. 1D space optimization.

name: Edit Distance (Insert, Delete, Replace)
notes: If s1[i] == s2[j]: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]. Else: 1 + min(insert: dp[i][j-1], delete: dp[i-1][j], replace: dp[i-1][j-1]).

name: Wildcard Matching ('?' and '*')
notes: If p[j]=='*': match 0 chars (dp[i][j-1]) or match 1 char and stay on * (dp[i-1][j]).

name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III & IV (At Most K Transactions)
notes: State: dp[day][buy][cap]. When sell executes, decrement cap by 1. Base case: cap == 0 or day == n.

name: Matrix Chain Multiplication (MCM)
notes: f(i, j) = min over k in [i, j-1] (f(i, k) + f(k+1, j) + arr[i-1]*arr[k]*arr[j]). Base case: i == j -> 0.

name: Burst Balloons
notes: Work in reverse: pick the LAST balloon k to burst in range [i, j]. Coins = nums[i-1]*nums[k]*nums[j+1] + dp(i, k-1) + dp(k+1, j).

name: Minimum Cost to Cut a Stick & Palindrome Partitioning II
notes: Sort cuts array and append [0, n]. dp[i][j] = (cuts[j] - cuts[i]) + min over k (dp[i][k] + dp[k][j]).

name: Palindrome Partitioning II (Minimum Cuts)
notes: dp[i] = min over j in [i, n-1] (1 + dp[j+1]) if s[i:j+1] is palindrome. Answer is dp[0] - 1.

name: Phase 8 Mastery Check: The 7 DP Archetypes
notes: Write out state transition equations for: 1) 0-1 Knapsack 2) LCS 3) Edit Distance 4) LIS 5) MCM. Review nuances.

name: Burst Balloons Benchmark
notes: Benchmark: Reconstruct the reverse burst intuition from a blank sheet.

name: Wildcard Matching Benchmark
notes: Benchmark: Handle '*' empty string match vs 1+ character match with 1D row array.

name: Evaluate Boolean Expression to True
notes: f(i, j, isTrue): split at operator k in [i+1, j-1] step 2. Combine left True/False with right True/False based on &, |, ^.

name: Maximal Rectangle with 1s
notes: Maintain heights array of size m. For each row: update height (if '1': height++, else: 0). Run Largest Rectangle in Histogram on heights.

name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock IV (At Most K Transactions)
notes: State dp[ind][buy][cap]. If buy: max(-prices[i] + f(i+1, 0, cap), f(i+1, 1, cap)). If sell: max(prices[i] + f(i+1, 1, cap-1), f(i+1, 0, cap)).

name: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
notes: Maintain min-heap of size k. If new element > heap[0], pop and push. Top is always the kth largest.

name: Shortest Job First (SJF) Waiting Time
